title: Quantaforge security and hosting discovery
topics: Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private deployment path
summary: Intro discovery call focused on security gating for an inference platform. Quantaforge is evaluating Redwood for a mix of hosted API usage for non-sensitive workloads and a Private/VPC deployment for PII-related models. Main open items: SOC2 evidence, SSO/SAML provisioning details, KMS options for BYOK, audit log retention and exportability, and a simple pricing/throughput check for dedicated capacity.

Samira Chen: Provide short runbook for SAML IdP setup and example metadata for Okta/Azure AD (due 2027-10-22)
Maya Lopez: Share expected RPS and sensitive model list so Redwood can scope Dedicated sizing (due 2027-10-26)

Quantaforge to send sample list of models that will touch PII and expected traffic profile

transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2027-10-19
Start: 16:00 UTC
Duration: ~52 minutes
Attendees: Jordan Patel (Redwood AE), Samira Chen (Redwood SE), Maya Lopez (Quantaforge CTO), Ethan Brooks (Quantaforge Security Engineer), Priya Nair (Quantaforge Head of Platform)

Summary / Notes (auto sections may be imperfect):
- Quick intro, objectives: understand security gating for production inference and hosting constraints.
- Quantaforge will likely use hosted for public-facing, non-PII models and Private (VPC) for PII/regulated models; interested in Dedicated for predictable throughput.
- Key asks: SOC2 evidence, SSO/SAML setup & SCIM, KMS / BYOK, audit log retention & export, RBAC granularity, data retention/ deletion semantics.

Transcript:
[00:00] Jordan (Redwood): Hey everyone, thanks for carving time—I'm Jordan, AE on the Redwood team. With me is Samira, our SE. How's it going, Maya?
[00:08] Maya (Quantaforge): Hi Jordan, hey Samira, thanks. We're juggling a few things but good to be here. Quick context: we run a hybrid inference platform at Quantaforge, some public models, but we have a set of models that process customer PII for finance use-cases. That's why security gating is huge for us.
[00:22] Samira (Redwood): Appreciate the context. We'll try to focus on the security and deployment options—hosted, dedicated, private—and the controls around encryption and identity.
[00:30] Ethan (Quantaforge): Quick intro from me — I'm Ethan, security engineer. Main things I want to cover: SOC2/ISO posture, how you do key management (BYOK?), SAML integration, and audit logging retention/export.
[00:39] Jordan: Perfect. Before we dive, high level — Redwood supports hosted API for fast time-to-value, Dedicated reservation for capacity, and Private VPC/on-prem for regulated workloads. We have SOC2 Type II and some customers run through our VPC private deployment when they need key separation.
[00:52] Maya: Are you SOC2 Type II today? I saw a blurb on the site but need artifacts.
[00:56] Jordan: Yes, we are. We'll share the Type II report and a controls matrix after this call. Note the report has redactions; we can also provide a controls mapping doc.
[01:10] Ethan: Good. For compliance we also need ISO 27001 evidence; do you have that or roadmaps?
[01:15] Samira: We're not ISO certified today; we're tracking a roadmap and can share the gap analysis. It's not blocking most of our customers who require ISO, but we can show compensating controls.
[01:25] Priya (Quantaforge): On identity — our org uses Okta and Azure AD in different business units. We need SSO via SAML and SCIM for provisioning. Also RBAC at team and environment level — we don't want devs calling production models.
[01:38] Samira: We integrate with SAML IdPs—Okta/Azure AD are common. We support SCIM for user provisioning. For RBAC we have role tiers: org-admin, team-admin, service-role. You can lock keys and set model-level access.
[01:50] Ethan: How granular is auditing? We need to track per-token usage, who invoked which model, and the raw request/response capturing is a no-go for PII.
[01:59] Jordan: Audit logs include API calls, model/version, token counts, and identity info. For Private deployments we can configure logs to be forwarded to the customer's SIEM — CloudWatch/Datadog/Splunk — and you can control retention. For hosted, we expose a logs export + retention policy; raw prompt/outputs are not stored beyond configured retention windows and PII can be redacted per retention policy.
[02:22] Maya: What's the default retention and can we set shorter windows? Also, does Redwood support customer-managed KMS for encrypting stored artifacts?
[02:31] Samira: Default retention for audit events is 90 days in hosted; we can shorten or extend with add-ons. For Private deployments, retention is whatever you configure in your environment. We support KMS integrations — cloud KMS (AWS KMS, GCP KMS) and BYOK with HSM-based key material. For hosted, BYOK is available in enterprise plans so keys are in your cloud account and we do key wrapping.
[02:53] Ethan: Key wrapping — can you explain how key access works for hosted? I need to understand if Redwood operators can decrypt.
[02:59] Samira: Sure — in hosted with BYOK, the customer owns the master key in their KMS. Redwood holds wrapped keys; runtime uses ephemeral keys that are unwrapped at the node level and never persisted unencrypted. Our operators do not have direct plaintext access to customer master keys.
[03:15] Jordan: To add — for the highest isolation we recommend Private/VPC where the control plane can be customer-managed and keys never leave the customer's network.
[03:23] Priya: For Private, do you offer an on-prem package or only VPC in cloud? We have some workloads that must not leave our AWS account.
[03:30] Samira: We have both options. VPC deployment in your AWS account is common—Redwood provides the control plane with customer-managed networking. For air-gapped on-prem, we have an enterprise package though that requires a deeper ops integration.
[03:42] Maya: SCIM provisioning — can Redwood integrate with multiple IdPs per org? We have mergers and multiple IdPs across business units.
[03:49] Jordan: Yes, multiple IdPs are supported; you can map IdP groups to Redwood roles. Samira will follow up with a setup runbook and example metadata.
[03:58] Ethan: Audit trail: can we get immutable logs and an export to our SIEM with signed attestations? Our compliance team will want tamper evidence.
[04:07] Samira: We can forward logs with signed delivery and we support WORM-like storage patterns via S3 + object lock when deployed in your account. For hosted, we have an append-only audit log service with integrity checks — we'll share the specifics in the artifact pack.
[04:22] Maya: Are there any residency constraints? We have EU customers; data must stay in EU.
[04:28] Jordan: Region pinning is supported. For hosted we operate in multiple cloud regions; you can pin requests to EU regions. For Private, obviously you choose the region/account.
[04:38] Priya: Ok on encryption in transit — TLS is fine — but what about model weights and caching on the inference nodes? Are those encrypted at rest?
[04:46] Samira: Yes weights and KV cache are encrypted at rest using the KMS you configure. For hosted deployments we use envelope encryption. Caches use in-memory when possible and disk caches are encrypted. There may be occasional mis-transcriptions in our docs where we call it K V cash, but it's cache.
[05:00] Ethan: Slightly different ask — we want to know what the rollback/fallback behavior is if a model variant is removed or a key rotation occurs. Any risk of downtime that leaks errors?
[05:10] Samira: We have automatic fallback policies. If a model variant is unavailable, requests can route to a compatible variant; for critical PII flows you'd typically route to a no-op or error path so you don't leak partial outputs. Key rotation is orchestrated — we support rolling rotations and dual-key phase to avoid decrypt errors.
[05:26] Jordan: Another practical item — pricing for Dedicated sizing. Priya, you said you want predictable throughput?
[05:32] Priya: Yes, we need predictable p95 latency and throughput for a billing reconciliation engine; spikes can be spiky so we want a buffer and possible burst capacity.
[05:41] Jordan: We can size Dedicated pools and offer reserved baseline + burst window. Samira will need your RPS and model sizes to make a recommendation.
[05:49] Maya: On legal — data retention and deletion: can you provide certified deletion for customer data on request? We need the ability to prove deletion.
[05:59] Samira: Yes, we provide deletion APIs and can provide attestations. For Private in your VPC, deletion is customer-controlled. For hosted, we can run deletion workflows and provide an audit of deletion events. Note that backups and analytic aggregates may have separate retention; we'll map that out in the controls matrix.
[06:17] Ethan: Anything else around firmware or hardware security? Some of our workloads will go on dedicated GPU hosts in Redwood Dedicated — we need info about hypervisor/SGX style protections.
[06:26] Samira: Our Dedicated hosts are isolated tenant-wise and we use kernel-level hardening. We don't currently rely on SGX, but we have confidential-compute proofs-of-concept. For the strictest assurances we recommend private deployment with HSMs in your network.
[06:40] Jordan: I'm going to go through the quick recap and then we can hand off action items.
[06:43] Jordan: Recap: Redwood is SOC2 Type II — we'll send the report; ISO in roadmap. SAML/SCIM supported and Samira to send runbook. KMS: BYOK + integration with AWS/GCP KMS and on-prem HSM in Private. Audit logs: forwardable to SIEM and configurable retention. RBAC: team-level roles and model-level gates. Next step: send artifacts and schedule SE deep dive.
[06:59] Maya: Sounds good. Would appreciate an explicit note on what is available in hosted vs dedicated vs private in one table — makes it easier for our procurement.
[07:07] Jordan: We'll attach a comparison sheet.
[07:09] Priya: One more thing — do you support tokenization / redaction at edge before logs are stored?
[07:16] Samira: Yes, there are hooks for pre-log redaction and masking at the proxy layer; we can include an example config.
[07:24] Ethan: Great. For the deep dive I'd like to go through an example provisioning flow with Okta and then a mock key rotation scenario.
[07:33] Jordan: Perfect, we'll set that up.
[07:35] Maya: Thanks team. We might have legal and procurement join the next call.
[07:39] Jordan: Noted. Any blocker for scheduling next week?
[07:41] Priya: No, next week works.
[07:43] Jordan: Cool. We'll send the artifacts and a calendar invite for the SE deep dive. Thanks all.

End of transcript (automated timestamps sometime imprecise).
